The spreadsheet gives one row per LimeSurvey question with the question code in its own 'id' column. The IRW code is that id, lower-cased after ^At?tInEx, with the build script's dmqReplacements applied. data/peters_2025_covid19_risk_dcts.py matches ^At?tIn(Ex|Ev)(.+)$ and lower-cases group 2, with no positional step. Two sheet ids carry the typo prefix 'AtInEx' (AtInExLoseRespect, AtInExWasteTime), which the At?t regex absorbs. Recorded as paper_explicit rather than data_labels for the same reason as the sibling: the sheet is a companion instrument-definition file, not the response export's header. STEP 3b: matches the table name and the dictionary Description ('Instrumental attitude items -- belief strength component (RAA)'). Every stem is a consequence-expectation stem ('If I keep at least {{distRec}} distance from others, I will ...'), not the evaluation stems ('I prefer to ...') of the sibling. CAVEAT 1 ({{distRec}} PLACEHOLDER KEPT VERBATIM): at run time LimeSurvey replaced it with the respondent's country's recommended distance, from the distRec sheet: 1 metre, 1.5 metres, 2 metres, 2.5 metres, 1 to 1.5 metres, 1 to 2 metres, or 6 feet. No single literal sentence is the item for every respondent. Shipping the study's own placeholder follows the SKILL rule for piped text and the pbc_cond_presence precedent (batch_134). CAVEAT 2 (ANCHOR NUMERALS STRIPPED): the rendered labels are the sheet's *_anchor_en, which append the displayed scale value ('save face (-3)' / 'lose respect (3)'; '... (1)' / '... (5)'). IRW ships the sheet's own *_anchor_bare variant. Bipolar items were displayed as -3..+3 and are stored as 1..7. CAVEAT 3 (INTERMEDIATE OPTIONS BLANK): only resp=1 and resp=max carry option_text; the intermediate DMQ_scales labels are bare numerals, so those rows are blank rather than padded. CAVEAT 4 (POOLED LANGUAGES): 22 cov_language codes in the live table (distinct respondent ids per code: en 18527, nl 15714, ro 2145, it 1106, pt-BR 861, tr 783, fr 334, es 224, id 179, el 140, pt 139, de 64, zh-Hans 31, hu 29, ar 23, am 18, pl 18, ja 12, zh-Hant-HK 11, ur 4, ko 2, he 1). language lists all 22 in that order, per the 2026-09-11 multi-language ruling. The batch_133/134 siblings predate that ruling and ship no language column, so this table deliberately differs from them. The base fields hold the English master text, which the English deployments read and which every other language version was translated from. So text_source=study_materials, and no _translated columns are emitted. CAVEAT 5 (AMENDED VARIANTS NOT IN THIS TABLE): amended wordings were added as separate LimeSurvey codes (questionId+'2') and are absent from the processing script's ITEM_POLARITY, so this table holds original-wording responses only. CAVEAT 6 (SOURCE QUIRKS KEPT VERBATIM): (a) two Flip twins repeat their partner's anchors rather than swapping them -- AttInExBiFlip (bi M=2.136, bifl M=2.089) and AttInExImplCompFlip (implcomp M=1.996, implcompfl M=2.097). The data agree the flip was never applied; a real flip would put them near 5.9 and 6.0. (b) the 'house' bottom anchor carries a double space ('infect people in my household  with the coronavirus'), transcribed as is. (c) Stems end with ' ...' in 53 rows and '...' with no space in four (othoffend, acteasy, outsideinf, contactfam), both as in the sheet. NO INSTRUCTIONS OR SECTION PROMPT: same finding as the batch_133 sibling -- the build script's add_group() supplies no group description, so none is published; both are left NA. Single trivial section_id; correct_response NA. VERIFY-SCRIPT CORRECTION WORTH CARRYING BACK: the batch_133 sibling's check D claims that reversing the anchor->code direction inverts its Flip-twin prediction. It does not: mean(flip) = (max+1) - mean(base) is invariant to a GLOBAL reversal. The twin test only establishes within-pair consistency. This table's verify script instead tests each pair's stated relation against its rival, and adds a content-based direction check (check E). The first draft, which used the sibling's fixed 0.30 tolerance, failed reasunifl at |d|=0.316 against a rival miss of 1.944. The sibling's own conclusion still stands on its build-script reading, but its evidence string overstates what check D shows. RETRY TEST: N/A, clean pass.
